Hosting the app on Posit Connect Cloud

Source: vignettes/articles/hosting.Rmd
hosting.Rmd

The synthcheck app can run on a server, so people can try it in a browser without installing R. This article walks through publishing it on Posit Connect Cloud from the GitHub repository. The same deploy/ folder also works on shinyapps.io with rsconnect::deployApp("deploy").

What changes on a server

run_synthcheck_app() on your own computer is not affected: It always runs the full app. The hosted app comes from synthcheck_app(hosted = TRUE) in deploy/app.R, and hosted mode differs in four ways:

  • No Ollama: Local models run on the visitor’s own computer, which a server cannot reach. The Models tab leaves Ollama out and says to install the package for local models. Anthropic, OpenAI and the mock provider work as usual.
  • Visitors bring their own keys: A key typed on the Models tab stays in that browser session’s memory and goes only to the provider. It is never saved on the server, in the files or in the R script. Keys in the server’s environment are never used, so a key you set there by mistake cannot pay for other people’s runs.
  • Files last one session: Each session writes its runs, interviews and response cache to its own temporary folder, which is deleted when the visitor closes the tab. Visitors download what they need from Export.
  • No Close button: Closing the app would stop it for everyone, so the Export tab offers the R script instead.

The About tab tells visitors all of this in a card at the top.

Hosted mode switches on when deploy/app.R sets it, when the option synthcheck.hosted is TRUE, when the environment variable SYNTHCHECK_HOSTED is true, or when the app detects shinyapps.io or Posit Connect.

Publish on Posit Connect Cloud

Connect Cloud publishes from a public GitHub repository. It reads deploy/app.R and a manifest.json beside it, which lists the packages and versions to install.

  1. Install synthcheck from GitHub on your computer, so the manifest records where the server gets it:

    remotes::install_github("okanbulut/synthcheck")
install.packages(c("rsconnect", "shiny", "bslib", "ellmer", "callr",
                   "jsonlite", "cicerone", "writexl", "readxl", "later",
                   "promises", "polycor"))

  2. Write the manifest from the root of your clone of the repository, and commit it:

    rsconnect::writeManifest("deploy")

    This creates deploy/manifest.json. Commit and push it to GitHub.

  3. Publish: Sign in at connect.posit.cloud with GitHub, choose Publish, then Shiny, and pick the repository okanbulut/synthcheck, the branch main and the primary file deploy/app.R. Do not add API keys under the settings for secrets or environment variables: The app does not use them.

  4. Try it: Open the link Connect Cloud gives you, choose the mock provider and run a short pretest. Then paste your own key and add one cheap model, such as claude-haiku-5-5 or gpt-4.1-nano.

Updating the hosted app

The manifest pins the synthcheck version from the commit you installed. After a new release, install synthcheck from GitHub again, run rsconnect::writeManifest("deploy") again, commit the new manifest and republish (or turn on publishing on each push in Connect Cloud).

Limits worth knowing

  • Long runs: A free server has little memory and stops an idle app. Keep hosted runs small (a few attempts and respondents) and run large studies in R on your own computer.
  • Costs: Every call is charged to the visitor’s own key. The app shows the estimated cost before a paid run and asks to confirm.
  • Privacy: Items, personas and answers are sent to the provider the visitor chooses, as they are in R.

The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.
